niches.title: Niches to search
niches.description: Which hardware-design niches to run. Each niche expands into 3-4 job-title search queries (see 'Custom queries' to override). Picking many niches at once, especially combined with multiple locations, adds up fast — LinkedIn's guest access can start getting rate-limited/walled at high volume even with pacing built in. Prefer a handful per run over one giant sweep.

customQueries.title: Custom queries (override niches)
customQueries.description: If set, these job-title search strings are used instead of the niche presets. One search string per line.

locations.title: Locations to search
locations.description: City / state / region / country strings, as you would type each one on LinkedIn. Every search query runs once per location listed here, so two locations roughly doubles the run's length and request volume. Default covers the US and Canada nationwide.

datePosted.title: Only jobs posted within
datePosted.description: Recency window. For a daily schedule, keep this at 'Past 24 hours'.

maxJobsPerQuery.title: Max jobs per query
maxJobsPerQuery.description: Cap on results pulled for each search string. 25 = one search page. Higher values page further into LinkedIn's results and take proportionally longer.

fetchFullDetails.title: Fetch full job details
fetchFullDetails.description: When ON, each unique posting gets one extra request to its LinkedIn job page for a real description, salary, industry and employment type (via LinkedIn's own structured job data). When OFF, only the search-result card fields are used (title, company, location, posted date) — faster and lighter, but thinner data.

excludeStaffingAgencies.title: Exclude staffing / recruiting agencies
excludeStaffingAgencies.description: Drop postings where the hiring company name looks like a staffing firm, recruiter or consultancy (you are one — these are competitors, not clients).

extraExcludeCompanies.title: Extra company names to exclude
extraExcludeCompanies.description: Additional company-name substrings to filter out (case-insensitive), e.g. your own firm and known competitors.

excludeTopCompanies.title: Exclude well-known large employers
excludeTopCompanies.description: Drop postings from a heuristic list of mega-cap tech, big semiconductor/EDA, and large aerospace/defense companies (Google, Microsoft, Intel, Qualcomm, Lockheed Martin, etc.) — they run their own in-house recruiting and generally aren't a staffing firm's target client. This is a backstop list, not exhaustive; the real size filter is below.

filterByCompanySize.title: Filter by company size (employee count)
filterByCompanySize.description: When ON, looks up each unique hiring company's LinkedIn-reported size band and drops postings above 'Max company size'. This is a best-effort lookup — LinkedIn's public company pages are inconsistently accessible (confirmed: a page that loads fine one moment can return a sign-up wall the next, with no clear pattern) — so a company whose size can't be confirmed is kept, not dropped, since guessing it away might mean losing a real lead. Turn OFF to skip the lookup entirely (faster, but no size targeting beyond the 'Exclude well-known large employers' list above).

maxCompanySize.title: Max company size (employees)
maxCompanySize.description: Upper bound on employee count for a posting's hiring company, when 'Filter by company size' is ON. LinkedIn reports size in bands (1-10, 11-50, 51-200, 201-500, 501-1,000, ...); 500 keeps everything through the 201-500 band and drops 501+.

onlyNewSinceLastRun.title: Output only jobs not seen in previous runs
onlyNewSinceLastRun.description: When ON, the dataset for this run contains only postings first seen today. When OFF, it contains every current match, each flagged is_new true/false. Keep OFF if the Google Sheet integration handles dedup.

descriptionSnippetLength.title: Job description snippet length (characters)
descriptionSnippetLength.description: How many characters of each job description to keep in the output row. 0 = drop descriptions entirely. Only applies when 'Fetch full job details' is ON.

googleSheetUrl.title: Google Sheet URL (optional, informational)
googleSheetUrl.description: Paste the URL of the Sheet you want rows appended to. Delivery is configured via the Apify → Google Sheets integration on this Actor/task (see README); this field is stored with the run for reference.
